dimensions.assessment: Affects all federal agencies conducting rulemakings under 5 U.S.C. 553(c), individuals and groups submitting public comments, OMB, GSA, and GAO.
dimensions.evidence: the head of an agency shall verify, to the greatest extent possible, at the time the comment is submitted, whether the comment has been submitted by a human being.

dimensions.assessment: Changes how public comments are processed, verified, and displayed on electronic dockets by allowing agencies to publish single representative copies of mass comments instead of every identical submission.
dimensions.evidence: instead of making available through the electronic docket of the agency each comment identified as a mass comment under paragraph (2), the head of an agency may make available through such docket only a single representative sample

dimensions.assessment: Requires GSA to update Regulations.gov and shared eRulemaking systems and agencies to update websites, but does not specify funding levels.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator of General Services, acting through the eRulemaking Program Management Office, shall update Regulations.gov as necessary

dimensions.assessment: Amends section 206 of the E-Government Act of 2002 to create new government-wide regulatory management mandates, OMB guidance requirements, and agency policy duties.
dimensions.evidence: To amend section 206 of the E-Government Act of 2002 to improve the integrity and management of mass comments and computer-generated comments

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent procedural requirements on federal rulemaking and docket management systems.

label: H.R. 9643

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 24 - 19.

other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 9643, Comment Integrity and Management Act

summary: H.R. 9643, the Comment Integrity and Management Act, sets requirements for how federal agencies handle mass comments and computer-generated comments during federal rulemakings. The bill requires agencies to verify whether public comments are submitted by human beings, identify mass comments, and decide how to display and consider these types of comments. It also mandates guidance from the Office of Management and Budget, website updates by the General Services Administration for Regulations.gov and the eRulemaking system, and a Government Accountability Office report.

affected_groups.effect: Must verify human submission of comments, identify and label mass comments, establish internal policies for handling computer-generated and mass comments, and update their websites and information systems.
Must issue implementation guidance for federal agencies regarding the management of mass and computer-generated comments.
Must update Regulations.gov and the eRulemaking system to ensure compliance with the bill's requirements.
Must study and report on the prevalence, identification, and effects of computer-generated comments in federal rulemakings within two years.
Will experience changes in how mass or computer-generated comments are displayed on public dockets, while mass comments remain explicitly recognized as a vital part of the regulatory process.

key_provisions: Requires federal agencies to verify, to the greatest extent possible when submitted, whether an electronic comment was submitted by a human being.
Requires agencies to identify mass comments and label them in a machine- and human-readable format on public dockets.

Allows agencies to publish a single representative sample or variation of a mass comment on the electronic docket rather than publishing every individual identical comment, provided they indicate the total number of identical or substantially identical submissions.
Directs the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with the General Services Administration, to issue implementation guidance within 240 days.
Requires each agency to establish and publish a policy on posting and considering computer-generated and mass comments within one year.
Requires the General Services Administration to update Regulations.gov and the shared eRulemaking system to ensure compliance within 18 months.
Requires the Government Accountability Office to submit a report within two years on the identification, prevalence, and effects of computer-generated comments in the rulemaking process.
missing_information: The specific technical methods or software tools agencies must use to verify human submissions are not detailed in the text.
The exact cost or budgetary appropriations required to update Regulations.gov, agency websites, and information systems are not specified.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9643, the Comment Integrity and Management Act, sets requirements for how federal agencies handle mass comments and computer-generated comments during federal rulemakings. The bill requires agencies to verify whether public comments are submitted by human beings, identify mass comments, and decide how to display and consider these types of comments. It also mandates guidance from the Office of Management and Budget, website updates by the General Services Administration for Regulations.gov and the eRulemaking system, and a Government Accountability Office report.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes procedural and technical requirements across the federal government for managing mass and AI- or computer-generated public comments on federal rules. Because it alters how large volumes of public input are processed, labeled, and displayed on public dockets while commissioning studies on computer-generated comments, its significance score reflects a moderate operational shift in federal rulemaking administration.
